records.title: Cook-Levin-Karp completeness spine
records.statement: SAT, CIRCUIT-SAT, 3-SAT and the audited Karp problems are NP-complete under explicit polynomial reductions; one NP-complete language in P implies P=NP.
hypotheses: Finite-string encodings and deterministic polynomial-time reduction model fixed by WP00.
Membership and hardness directions are both supplied.
records.conclusion: A correct polynomial-time decider for any locked NP-complete language composes to the equality terminal target.
records.source_locator: Cook theorem and Karp reduction catalogue; per-problem encoding certificate required
residual_hypotheses: Exact reduction certificate and bit-size bound for each selected representative.
records.claim_boundary: Completeness transfers a proved algorithm or lower bound; it supplies neither.

records.title: 2-SAT tractability
records.statement: 2-SAT admits a deterministic linear-time decision algorithm under standard explicit formula encodings.
hypotheses: Every clause has at most two literals.
The implication graph is represented explicitly.
records.conclusion: The restricted language 2-SAT lies in P.
residual_hypotheses: No reduction from unrestricted SAT to 2-SAT preserving satisfiability in polynomial size is supplied.
records.claim_boundary: A tractable syntactic subclass does not decide unrestricted SAT.

records.title: Horn-SAT tractability
records.statement: Horn satisfiability admits a deterministic linear-time forward-chaining algorithm under explicit Horn encodings.
hypotheses: Every clause contains at most one positive literal.
residual_hypotheses: No coverage theorem for arbitrary CNF is supplied.
records.claim_boundary: Horn tractability is not a P=NP result.

records.title: Schöning fixed-k randomized local search
records.statement: For fixed k, randomized local search with restart solves satisfiable k-SAT with an exponential expected running-time improvement over exhaustive search.
hypotheses: Randomness and expected or high-probability runtime are retained.
records.conclusion: A nontrivial randomized exponential-time algorithm exists for fixed-k SAT.
residual_hypotheses: Polynomial—not merely improved exponential—worst-case time is absent.
records.claim_boundary: An improved exponential randomized algorithm does not place SAT in P.

records.title: PPSZ fixed-k randomized algorithm
records.statement: PPSZ gives improved randomized exponential-time bounds for fixed-k SAT, with exact guarantees depending on uniqueness and algorithm variant.
hypotheses: Randomized success and amplification costs are charged.
Formula class and uniqueness promises are explicit.
records.conclusion: A structured randomized exponential-time SAT algorithm is available for fixed k.
records.source_locator: JACM theorem statements; variant-specific constants require per-use extraction
residual_hypotheses: No removal of promise or randomness without theorem.
records.claim_boundary: PPSZ is not a polynomial-time SAT decider.

records.title: ETH and SETH conditional framework
records.statement: ETH and SETH formulate quantitative lower-bound hypotheses for SAT and related problems; consequences are conditional on those hypotheses.
hypotheses: The selected ETH or SETH formulation is stated exactly.
Reduction preserves the exponent and parameter regime claimed.
records.conclusion: Conditional fine-grained lower bounds and transfer theorems may be derived.
records.source_locator: Subexponential reduction framework; SETH variants require separate sources
residual_hypotheses: P!=NP alone does not supply ETH or SETH.
records.claim_boundary: A conditional consequence cannot be promoted as an unconditional P-versus-NP theorem.

records.title: Karp-Lipton nonuniform collapse interface
records.statement: If NP is contained in P/poly, then the polynomial hierarchy collapses to its second level.
hypotheses: The standard polynomial hierarchy is used.
records.conclusion: A strong nonuniform upper bound has a hierarchy-collapse consequence.
records.model: nonuniform Boolean circuits and uniform hierarchy classes
residual_hypotheses: P/poly membership does not itself produce a uniform polynomial-time algorithm.
The converse collapse implication is unavailable.
records.claim_boundary: Nonuniform circuits and uniform P must not be interchanged.

records.title: Nondeterministic time hierarchy
records.statement: Appropriately separated nondeterministic time bounds define distinct classes.
hypotheses: Time-constructibility and separation conditions are met.
The diagonal language remains in the stated larger class.
records.conclusion: A hierarchy separation is obtained for the specified time classes.
residual_hypotheses: No theorem places the separated language in NP while excluding all polynomial time.
records.claim_boundary: Time hierarchy alone does not separate P from NP.
